problem.title: Business opportunity is often lost in translation.
problem.description: Businesses usually know the outcome they want. They do not always know the right provider category, capability term, procurement language, or evidence to request. Capable providers face the same problem in reverse.

items.title: “I know what I need—but not what to call it.”
items.detail: A business problem rarely arrives with the correct classification already attached.

items.title: “We can do the work—but customers describe it differently.”
items.detail: Similar capabilities can be expressed through different industries, services, and terminology.

items.title: “A directory tells me who exists—not always who fits.”
items.detail: Names, websites, and industry codes are useful, but they do not fully connect a specific need with the capability required.

items.title: “The context disappears as the process moves.”
items.detail: Email, spreadsheets, referrals, support programs, and bid systems often hold different pieces of the same need.

problem.closing: The RFxchange is designed to reduce that translation gap.

how.eyebrow: From ordinary language to market action

amacs.title: A common language for market activity.
amacs.description: The RFxchange uses the Accel Market Activity and Capability Standard—AMACS—to connect more than what a business sells or which industry it belongs to.
amacs.support: AMACS gives the Exchange a common way to connect what the market needs with what organizations can actually do.

nodes.title: Need
nodes.detail: What is the market trying to accomplish?

nodes.title: Capability
nodes.detail: What must a provider be able to do?

nodes.title: Response
nodes.detail: What information does the market need back?

amacs.futureNote: Need and capability are already central to the current product. RFx, decision, credibility, and outcome expressions remain later governed pathways.

ai.title: AI can suggest. People confirm.
ai.description: AI can reduce the burden of turning ordinary descriptions into structured market information. It may suggest relevant AMACS concepts and explain possible relationships—but a suggestion is not a market fact.
ai.highlight: An authorized participant confirms what the organization actually needs, provides, or represents before authoritative state changes.
principles: Ordinary language remains an acceptable starting point.
The model cannot invent AMACS identifiers or silently create claims.
Rejected or unresolved suggestions cannot affect authoritative discovery or matching.
Manual AMACS browse and search remain available when assistance is disabled or unavailable.

network.title: See the market around your business.
network.description: The RFxchange begins with a real organization in a real place. After activation, the organization receives a real or privacy-safe map position and can become discoverable through confirmed market information.

items.title: Find businesses by capability.
items.detail: Search for what organizations can do—not only what they are called.

items.title: Use geography as business context.
items.detail: Understand where participating organizations are based and the areas they are authorized to serve.

items.title: Open the organization behind the marker.
items.detail: Move from location into permitted capability, service, and organization context.

items.title: Move from discovery into action.
items.detail: Create consented referrals and provider connections without representing discovery itself as an outcome.

network.imageNote: Atmospheric image—not live RFxchange market evidence.

trust.title: Credibility should come from evidence—not payment.
trust.description: RFxchange separates business claims, public-source information, provider approval, verification, connections, commercial recognition, and outcomes instead of collapsing them into a single badge.
trust.highlight: Paid membership, Founding recognition, or sponsorship does not buy better capability matching, verification, qualification, or preferred placement in neutral discovery.
rules: A self-reported capability is not automatically verified.
Official Resource Provider status is an approved institutional role—not a guarantee of fit or availability.
A referral or provider connection is not a completed service or successful outcome.
Future credibility and outcome signals must identify their evidence and authority.

why.title: You do not have to wait for the entire Exchange to create value.
why.description: The first useful step is to make your organization understandable to the market. The clearer its confirmed capabilities and context become, the more useful later discovery and transaction workflows can be.

items.title: Establish your position early
items.detail: Create or claim the organization, confirm its geography, and build a structured capability position before the wider transaction engine opens.

items.title: Help shape practical workflows

items.title: Contribute to a better market language

items.title: Be recognized as part of the launch cohort

scenario.eyebrow: The problem we are building around
scenario.title: Business owners should not need procurement expertise to explain a business need.
scenario.quote: “We have outgrown the way we manage inventory and need help figuring out a better system.”
scenario.description: That statement may involve process analysis, inventory technology, systems integration, data migration, training, workflow design, or several capabilities together. RFxchange is being built so the business can begin with the problem it understands and then confirm useful structure.

standard.title: AI helps with the translation. AMACS provides the structure. People provide the authority.
standard.description: AMACS connects Need, Capability, Evidence, Response, Decision, and Outcome. AI may suggest relevant concepts, but it does not decide what your company can do, silently create a requirement, or declare another organization qualified.
standard.highlight: Suggestions reduce the work. Authorized people confirm the market facts.

boundaries.title: Money does not make a business a better match.

items.title: No pay-to-rank
items.detail: Founding status does not move an organization above a more relevant participant in neutral discovery.

items.title: No pay-to-verify
items.detail: Membership does not establish that a capability, credential, or business claim is true.

items.title: No pay-to-qualify
items.detail: Founding status cannot substitute for the requirements of a particular opportunity.

items.title: No guaranteed business
items.detail: RFxchange does not guarantee leads, referrals, contracts, revenue, awards, financing, or growth.

boundaries.closing: Commercial benefits and market truth remain separate by design.

items.question: Do I need to know how to write an RFP?
items.answer: No. RFxchange is broader than formal procurement. You can begin with the need you understand; later RFx workflows will add the appropriate transaction structure.

items.question: Do I need to understand AMACS codes?
items.answer: No. You may browse structured concepts, but ordinary-language assistance and explanations are designed to make the standard usable without memorizing a taxonomy.

items.question: Does Founding participation make my business Verified?
items.answer: No. Founding Organization is launch-cohort recognition. Verification requires the applicable governed evidence and verification process.

items.question: Will Founding membership improve my search ranking?
items.answer: No. Payment does not change substantive capability truth, neutral matching, qualification, or credibility.

items.question: Is the entire RFxchange platform live?
items.answer: No. The Wave 3 Network is live. RFx Core, evaluation, credibility, outcomes, and paid entitlements remain later governed pathways.

items.question: Why participate before everything is complete?
items.answer: Because useful market positioning begins before the final transaction engine. You can establish structured organization information now while helping identify where later workflows need improvement.

items.question: How is AI used?
items.answer: AI may help interpret ordinary language and suggest relevant AMACS concepts. Suggestions remain non-authoritative until an authorized participant takes the applicable confirming action.

items.question: What if AMACS does not describe something my business does?
items.answer: Do not force an incorrect classification. Preserve the unresolved meaning and use the governed provisional-term and review pathway where available.

items.question: Can I still participate without becoming a Founder?
items.answer: Yes. Useful free organization participation is intentional. Founding is a deeper launch layer, not a tollbooth in front of legitimate network activity.
